prompt:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of Kameosa, the auspicious Japanese water-jar yokai with inexhaustible water.
ANATOMY: ONE ancient broad earthenware WATER JAR with TWO large solemn dark EYES, ONE broad NOSE and ONE strong closed MOUTH formed naturally in worn ceramic; no head separate from vessel, NO arms, legs, teeth or horns. Face carved-looking but alive, stern wise benevolent expression [kameosa-c02].
MOMENT: The great old jar leans against a timber wall, tilting its rim forward so a huge continuous TORRENT OF CLEAR WATER crashes into three already overflowing plain wooden basins and across the foreground floor. Its eyes stare intently down toward viewer; mouth remains below rim and water comes from TOP OPENING. One plain ladle rests visibly across rim.
POWER: water never runs out however much is ladled, impossible continuous abundance, jar remains visibly brim-full despite torrent; no levitation, water serpents, magical glow or beams [kameosa-c03,kameosa-c07].
SCALE & CAMERA: extreme low near-floor close angle; expressive ceramic jar and towering sheet of physical water dominate square, ordinary household jar size relative to basins, not invented giant.
LIGHT & WEATHER: one warm off-frame hearth source sharply rims wet pottery and translucent water, deep walnut interior shadows, physical spray and droplets.
SURFACE: cracked rough dark ochre ceramic, mineral stains, wet carved facial ridges, worn basins and splintered timber.
SETTING: editorial old Japanese household water corner; no specific site asserted.
MOOD: imposing benevolent uncanny bounty and wonder [kameosa-c13], never evil, cute smiling mascot, static jar or calm still life.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text, lettering, inscriptions, logo, border, frame or watermark; no extra heads, limbs or fingers; no design borrowed from any film, game, anime or comic; no nudity or explicit gore; no generic glow aura, neon outline or energy ribbons. Premium painterly brushwork, dark warm walnut and antique gold palette, square composition.
name: Kameosa
rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.

visual_review.notes: Native and 200px inspected: living faced ceramic water jar with exactly two eyes/nose/mouth, no limbs invented. Jar remains full while large torrent spills from top into three brimming basins; ladle at rim. Physical abundance is active and imposing at thumbnail; solemn benevolent face no evil traits. No text, cute mascot, extra anatomy or aura. Seven Sangar checks pass.

root_visual_review.notes: Viewed native 1254px + 200px + face crop. A single old earthenware water jar turned tsukumogami, its surface forming a face with exactly two eyes, a broad nose and a solemn mouth (kameosa-c02/c03) — no invented arms, legs or extra features. An endless torrent of water pours from the jar and overflows several wooden basins and across the floor, the inexhaustible supply (kameosa-c05). Dignified, weathered, non-malicious expression — an awe-inspiring spirit of good fortune, not a cute mascot (kameosa-c12/c13) — in an old sake-brewery storehouse with a resting ladle. No lettering on the jar, no glow aura, no copied Sekien woodblock; an original premium painterly interpretation. Awe through impossible abundance; reads clearly at 200px.
